stepNotes.1: The two React exports, one pure diff export, and its test are wired through App.tsx:953-965 and Header.tsx:1788-1804, connecting synchronized sessions to native, badge, and in-app notification surfaces.
stepNotes.2: Permission tool names and patterns are untrusted request data but render only as escaped React text; fixed response literals and captured IDs flow through session-actions.ts:922-937 with directory ownership resolution.
stepNotes.3: The Set-based diff adds unseen request IDs and removes mappings absent from the live list; the watcher applies both halves and clears all mapped notifications during unmount.
stepNotes.4: Medium defect: NotificationCenter removes an item immediately while the response promise runs; on rejection the request stays pending but its mirror-map entry blocks re-creation, unlike PermissionCard's await-and-retry lifecycle.
stepNotes.5: Native delivery rechecks focused-session state after a cancellable two-second delay, one notification covers a continuous waiting episode, and attention counts are cleared from both web and desktop state on unmount.
stepNotes.6: Store history is capped at 100 and reconciliation is linear, but the memoized relative-time label has no clock dependency and can remain stale throughout an idle open-panel interval.
stepNotes.7: Pure reconciliation is isolated from React effects and all displayed copy is localized; the dialog restores focus and handles Escape, but lacks aria-modal and focus containment despite using a backdrop.
stepNotes.8: Four tests cover diff additions, stale removal, preservation, and empty input; component behavior, debounce cleanup, badge cleanup, rejected responses, and dialog keyboard boundaries have no direct tests.
stepNotes.9: Package-local Vitest passed 1 file and 4 tests and package type-check passed; the review accepts one Medium and two Low issues, finds no Critical evidence, and therefore creates no reverify.md.
